subject: Spanska
title: Comparisons and daily life
sourceSummary: Comparing things (más/menos que, tan... como) and vocabulary for a typical day.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct comparison: "Mi hermano es ___ alto ___ yo." (My brother is taller than me.)
questions.opener: "More ... than" is formed with más ... que.
questions.explanation: "Más ... que" means "more ... than": "más alto que yo" = "taller than me". "Tan ... como" is used instead for "as ... as".

questions.prompt: What does "Este libro es tan interesante como el otro" mean?
choices: This book is more interesting than the other one
This book is less interesting than the other one
This book is just as interesting as the other one
This book is the most interesting
questions.explanation: "Tan ... como" means "as ... as": the books are equally interesting.

questions.prompt: Which word is irregular in the comparative ("better")?
questions.opener: Just like Swedish's "good – better" is irregular.
questions.explanation: "Bueno" (good) has the irregular comparative form "mejor" (better), not "más bueno". Likewise, "malo" (bad) → "peor" (worse).

questions.prompt: What does "Me levanto a las siete" mean?
questions.opener: Reflexive verbs are often used for daily routines.
choices: I go to bed at seven
questions.explanation: "Levantarse" means "to get up/rise", and "me levanto" is the present-tense form for "I": "I get up at seven".

questions.prompt: What does "Me acuesto a las diez y media" mean?
questions.opener: Another common reflexive verb for daily routines.
choices: I shower at half past ten
I go to bed at half past ten
I eat dinner at half past ten
I leave home at half past ten
questions.explanation: "Acostarse" means "to go to bed", and "me acuesto" is "I go to bed": "I go to bed at half past ten".

questions.prompt: Write the Spanish word for "to shower" in its base form (infinitive).
Correct the error: "Mi casa es más pequeña que la tuya, pero mi jardín es más bueno."
questions.opener: "Bueno" has its own irregular comparative form.
questions.answer: Mi casa es más pequeña que la tuya, pero mi jardín es mejor.
steps: "Más bueno" is incorrect — bueno conjugates irregularly in the comparative.
The correct form is "mejor" (better), without "más" in front.
The full sentence: "Mi casa es más pequeña que la tuya, pero mi jardín es mejor." (My house is smaller than yours, but my garden is better.)

questions.prompt: How do you form comparisons and describe a daily routine in Spanish?
questions.opener: Comparison words and reflexive verbs for everyday life.
questions.answer: Comparisons: más ... que = more ... than · menos ... que = less ... than · tan ... como = as ... as · mejor/peor = better/worse (irregular). Daily routine (reflexive verbs): despertarse = to wake up · levantarse = to get up · ducharse = to shower · vestirse = to get dressed · desayunar = to eat breakfast · acostarse = to go to bed. Reflexive pronouns: me, te, se, nos, os, se — placed before the verb: me levanto, te levantas, se levanta.

questions.prompt: What does "menos caro que" mean in a comparison between two products?
questions.opener: "Menos ... que" is the opposite of "más ... que".
questions.explanation: "Menos caro que" means "less expensive than", the opposite of "más caro que" (more expensive than).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct superlative form: "Este restaurante es ___ de la ciudad." (This restaurant is the best in the city.)
questions.opener: "Bueno" has an irregular superlative form, just like in the comparative.
questions.explanation: The superlative form of "bueno" is "el mejor" (the best), not "el más bueno". The same irregularity as in the comparative (mejor).

questions.prompt: What does "Me cepillo los dientes después de desayunar" mean?
questions.opener: "Cepillarse los dientes" is a reflexive expression for brushing your teeth.
choices: I brush my teeth after breakfast
I eat breakfast after brushing my teeth
questions.explanation: "Me cepillo los dientes después de desayunar" means "I brush my teeth after breakfast".

questions.prompt: What does "Normalmente salgo de casa a las ocho" mean?
questions.opener: "Normalmente" signals a recurring habit, not a one-time event.
choices: I usually leave home at eight
I sometimes leave home at eight
I left home yesterday at eight
I'm going to leave home at eight
questions.explanation: "Normalmente salgo de casa a las ocho" means "I usually leave home at eight" — a description of a regular routine.

questions.prompt: Which word is irregular in the superlative for "bad" (the worst)?
questions.opener: "Malo", just like "bueno", has an irregular superlative form.
questions.explanation: The superlative form of "malo" is "el peor" (the worst), not "el más malo".

questions.prompt: Which reflexive pronoun fits "nosotros"? "___ levantamos temprano los lunes." (We get up early on Mondays.)
questions.opener: Reflexive pronouns follow the same pattern as personal pronouns: yo-me, tú-te, nosotros-nos.
questions.explanation: "Nos" is the reflexive pronoun for "nosotros" (we): "nos levantamos" means "we get up".

questions.prompt: How do you express that two things are exactly the same size, e.g. "Mi casa es ___ grande ___ la tuya"?
questions.opener: Similarity is expressed with "tan ... como", not "más" or "menos".
questions.explanation: "Tan ... como" means "as ... as": "mi casa es tan grande como la tuya" = "my house is as big as yours".
